title.narrative: CERF Emergency Rapid Response to flood-affected populations in Borno, Bauchi, and Sokoto states, Nigeria

description.narrative: Maiduguri Metropolis which comprises Maiduguri, Jere, and some parts of Konduga and Mafa local government areas (LGAs) in Borno State, Nigeria, has experienced severe flooding due to the collapse of the Alau Dam, in mid-September 2024. The flooding has submerged much of the city, damaging infrastructure, including homes, hospitals, and schools. The Sanda Kyarimi Zoo also suffered significant losses, with some animals escaping, posing additional risks to residents. IOM through the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), in collaboration with the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the Borno State Emergency Management Agency (BOSEMA), and the Nigerian Red Cross Society (NRCS), identified 138 locations in Borno State that were impacted by floods or received internally displaced persons (IDPs) due to the flooding. In the 19 LGAs of Borno State that were assessed, DTM identified 320,791 individuals in 65,731 households affected by the floods. In Bauchi State, 114 locations were impacted by floods or received IDPs due to the flooding. Assessments identified 57,827 individuals in 9,620 flood-affected households. A similar assessment was also conducted by DTM in 10 LGAs of Sokoto where 56,308 individuals were identified in 10,808 households affected by the floods. These individuals included people displaced by the floods and residents impacted by the floods but remained in their communities. In total, 434,926 individuals in 86,159 households were affected by the flooding across Borno, Bauchi and Sokoto states.However, concerns about waterborne diseases and food shortages have also emerged. The Government of Nigeria, along with the state governor and agencies like SEMA, NEMA, and international organizations, is coordinating relief efforts, including the provision of funds and supplies to assist those affected.For this project, IOM will provide support to the flood affected populations in Borno, Bauchi, and Sokoto states through the provision of multisectoral services including shelter and non-food items (NFIs), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), early recovery, camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) and multi-purpose cash assistance.
